snippet.title: Jev + Claude = INSANE Results (Every Concept Explained)
snippet.description:
🚀 Join the Agentic Academy: https://skool.com/scrapes
 👀 Be the brand AI recommends: https://dub.sh/rankspot-yt
 📋 Free Jev resources: https://skool.com/scrapesai 
 Don't miss the next build - https://www.youtube.com/@simonscrapes?sub_confirmation=1

Typesafe just released Jev, a "judgment model" that can't write a sentence and can't chat, and in its first week people used it to build a browser agent that fills in Google Flights in seconds and to sort 3 million website sessions for about $2. In this video, I go through the official docs so you don't have to. I cover how Jev turns messy inputs into calibrated probabilities, the three question types (yes/no, choice and score), why it's 40 to 1,000x cheaper and much faster than LLMs, and how it works alongside Claude rather than replacing it. Then we install the Typesafe skill in Claude Code and build a live customer support triage system that sorts 50 emails into four piles in 4 seconds for a fraction of a cent. We finish with the four patterns from the docs for getting the most out of it: speculative fan-out, confidence-gated routing, weighted scoring and intent routing.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Intro: The AI model that can't write a sentence
00:46 1: What it is: a judgement model
03:31 2: Why it's special compared to LLMs
05:16 3: It replaces one job Claude does, not Claude
06:23 4: Noul — the yes/no that comes back as a probability
07:29 5: Choice — pick one, and see the odds on all of them
08:04 6: Confidence — the second number, and the one that decides
09:20 7: Score — for when the options have an order
11:04 8: Which type, and all three in one request
12:40 9: In front of Claude — the guard that reads everything first
14:22 10: The skill is a rulebook, not a tool
18:31 11: Start from the action, not from the data
23:52 12: State — named fields, and nothing else
25:36 13: Extra questions are almost free
29:02 14: The checklist for finding your own Jev steps
32:13 15: Pattern 1: ask everything at once
33:10 16: Pattern 2: confidence-gated routing
34:05 17: Pattern 3: score the parts, weight them yourself
35:07 18: Pattern 4: route it to the best handler for that job
35:54 19: All four together: the smart home demo
